title: Why Do Cargo Ships Have a Giant Bulb on the Front?

scenes.text: Look at the front of any massive cargo ship, and you will find something that makes no sense.
A giant steel bulb, bolted to the very bottom of the bow.
It looks like damage that nobody bothered to fix.
So why would engineers add a huge lump of steel to the fastest part of the ship?
Because a moving ship pushes a wave up in front of itself, and that wave is wasted energy.
The bulb sits ahead of the hull, and it makes a second wave of its own.
The two waves collide, cancel each other out, and the water goes almost flat.
Less wave means less drag, and less drag can cut fuel use by fifteen percent.
On a ship burning a hundred tons of fuel a day, that ugly bulb pays for itself in one voyage.
